## Results

- Eight strategies backtested over 19 years (2007-2026) at 1 bp costs: none beat buy-and-hold SPY on return (10.68% CAGR)
- The Faber 200-day moving-average filter cut maximum drawdown from -55.2% to -24.6% while keeping 90% of the return (9.59% CAGR)
- Faber Sharpe 0.65 against 0.51 for buy-and-hold, a difference that does not clear a block-bootstrap interval of [-0.21, +0.49]. The drawdown reduction is the durable finding, not the return
- Oscillator signals underperformed: RSI mean reversion Sharpe 0.11, MACD cross 0.43 at 42x annual turnover
- The live alerting pipeline runs on point-in-time SEC EDGAR fundamentals, filtered to filing date so no signal sees data before it was public

## The problem

A long-horizon, tax-sheltered account must choose between passive buy-and-hold and tactical rules (trend filters, momentum, oscillator signals). Popular signals are widely promoted, but whether they improve risk-adjusted outcomes after costs is an empirical question.

## What I built

I wrote a vectorized daily engine that applies each strategy's target weights to adjusted ETF prices (SPY, EFA, IEF, GSG, VNQ, AGG, with BIL as cash) from May 2007 to May 2026. Every strategy shares the same dates, cost model of 1 bp per side, and cash proxy, and is scored on CAGR, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, maximum drawdown, Calmar and turnover against buy-and-hold SPY. The signals come from HedgeAbove, a cron-driven rule engine I run on a Raspberry Pi with SQLite deduplication, Telegram delivery, point-in-time SEC EDGAR fundamentals and walk-forward threshold selection.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Frames an allocation choice as decision analysis under uncertainty: state the criterion, which here is drawdown and risk-adjusted return rather than raw CAGR, test the alternatives on equal terms, and accept the answer the data gives.
:::

## Tools

Python, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, yfinance, Streamlit, Plotly, SQLite, SEC EDGAR XBRL (edgartools), FRED, Telegram Bot API, Raspberry Pi cron

[A personal research project, not investment advice.]{.fine}
